Hey team — technical breakdown below and a short proposed clause at the end. Leaving legal polish to Marissa.

Technical summary (current Hosted + Dedicated behaviors):
- Local cache: We use ephemeral prefix/KV caches to accelerate token generation. Caches may contain prompt prefixes and intermediate decoder state, but not long-term storage of full request logs unless telemetry is enabled.
- Retention: default cache TTLs are short (typically 30s–5m depending on model/latency profile). Telemetry logs (request metadata + sampling of tokens for diagnostics) are retained 30 days in Hosted by default; Dedicated customers can request retention adjustments in contract.
- Opt-outs: For Dedicated tenants, we can disable sampling of request payloads for telemetry and restrict access to telemetry pipelines. For Hosted tenants, full opt-out is harder without a Dedicated plan or contract amendment.
- Downstream processors: We do use subprocessors (analytics, observability) but only under contract with appropriate processor obligations and data flow restrictions; we do not 'sell' data for advertising or monetization.

Proposed short clause for DPA/US Addendum (draft):
"Redwood will act only as a Service Provider or Processor with respect to Customer Personal Information and shall not sell Personal Information as defined under CCPA/CPRA. Redwood may engage Subprocessors for performance, hosting, analytics, and observability; such Subprocessors will be bound by written agreements that limit their use to performing services on behalf of Redwood and prohibit sale or independent commercial use of Customer Personal Information.

Redwood's runtime may use short-lived in-memory caching and operational telemetry to provide and improve the Service. Redwood will not persist customer request payloads in durable storage for longer than established telemetry retention periods, and will provide, for Dedicated customers, options to reduce or disable sampling of request payloads used in telemetry pipelines. Specific retention periods and opt-out options will be defined in the Service Order or Addendum for Dedicated deployments."

Attachments referenced: cache_design_summary.pdf (internal design + TTLs), redwood-proposed-dpa-clause.txt (draft clause).

If Marissa is comfortable with that wording, we can send to HealthApp with an option: (A) include clause as-is for Hosted (adds "no sale" and subprocessor limits + standard telemetry notes) or (B) include Clause + Dedicated addendum paragraph offering reduced telemetry/sampling and shorter retention windows.

— Karthik

Hi Amelia — thanks for the clear redlines and timeline. Appreciate the patient review.

We've reviewed internally and can confirm Redwood's position and proposed language below. Broadly: Redwood will act as a Service Provider / Processor and will not 'sell' Customer Personal Information under CPRA/CCPA. We do use short-lived caching and telemetry for performance and diagnostics, but Durable persistence of request payloads is not our default behavior and Dedicated customers can contractually reduce or disable sampling.

Proposed addition to your US Privacy Addendum (suggested paragraph):
"No Sale; Subprocessors; Transient Caching and Telemetry. Redwood represents and warrants that it will act as a Service Provider or Processor with respect to Customer Personal Information and will not sell Personal Information as defined by applicable U.S. privacy laws. Redwood may engage Subprocessors (for hosting, analytics, monitoring, and support) necessary to provide the Service; such Subprocessors shall be subject to written agreements that prohibit sale or independent commercial use of Customer Personal Information. Redwood's runtime may use transient, in-memory caching and limited telemetry sampling to provide and improve the Service. Redwood will not persist full request payloads in durable storage longer than the telemetry retention period specified in the Service Order, and, for Dedicated Customers, Redwood will offer options to reduce or disable sampling of request payloads and adjust retention windows as specified in the Service Order or Addendum."

If that looks reasonable to you, we can prepare a redline back to your attached DPA. If HealthApp requires a hard commit to zero-sampling for production traffic (no telemetry of any request payloads), that is typically scoped to Dedicated customers and will need an explicit Service Order + a short implementation window (we estimate 4–8 weeks engineering work to fully block sampling pipelines for a tenant and provide operational runbooks).

Next steps suggested:
- If HealthApp accepts the proposed paragraph, we'll send a redline (DocuSign-ready) and flag the telemetry options in the Service Order.
- If HealthApp requires zero-sampling for Hosted, we'll need to triage with Product and provide a timeline/cost estimate.

DocuSign link (prelim): https://www.docusign.com/links/HS-8902-DPA

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if you prefer.

Best,
Soojin Lee
